text:
New Jersey won 4-1, and the scoreboard undersold how one-sided the night was. The Devils attempted 64 shots to Vancouver's 42, put 37 on goal to 21, and took 76 percent of the simulated replays. Three of their four goals came on the power play, where they went 3 for 4 against Vancouver's 1 for 3, and the man advantage was worth 1.33 expected goals to the Canucks' 0.29.

Linus Karlsson gave Vancouver the lead at 5:27 of the first on a power-play snap shot, but it lasted less than three minutes. Nico Hischier tied it at 8:03 with his own power-play goal, and Jesper Boqvist put New Jersey ahead at 16:24 with a wrist shot at even strength, a 27 percent chance. Jesper Bratt made it 3-1 at 4:36 of the second, and Hischier added a snap shot with ten seconds left in the period for the fourth. Hischier finished with two goals and an assist, and Bratt had a goal and an assist. Hischier's line was on the ice for 2.04 expected goals for and 0.83 against.

Jake Allen was the first star without a point to his name. He stopped 20 of 21 shots, saving 1.35 goals more than the chances deserved, and Karlsson's goal was the only one to beat him. Vancouver's Leevi Meriläinen gave up three on 34 shots and was roughly even with expectation. Kevin Lankinen allowed one on three shots in relief. Jake DeBrusk fired seven shots on goal for the Canucks, but they never found a way to turn that into more than one goal.
